thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High packet loss detected to eu-west via ProviderX (AS64512). Automated thresholds breached for: 1) inter-region latency spike, 2) packet loss >20% for multiple prefixes. Paging on-call network + on-call SRE.

alex: I'm on it. seeing a lot of tcp retransmits to 185.45.12.0/22 from eu-west1. metrics -> 35-60% packet loss during 14:06-14:12 UTC.

sophia: confirmed from neteng side, BGP flap observed with ProviderX neighbors. Flap count jumped. suspect upstream route instability.

mike: alex / sophia — are customer-facing products impacted? any 5xx spikes?

carla: checked observability: hosted-api error rate up ~22% in eu-west region, long tails on connections -> upstream connection failures. Affected: streaming and chat endpoints with persistent connections.

alex: quick dump from edge v4 router (excerpt):
```
# show bgp neighbors
BGP neighbor is 203.0.113.10, remote AS 64512,  established 00:00:54, flaps 7
  Neighbor capabilities: route-refresh, 4Byte, as4
  Received prefixes 1200, advertised 0
BGP neighbor is 203.0.113.11, remote AS 64512,  established 00:00:12, flaps 9
```

alex: and tcpdump from edge -> lots of ICMP unreachable + retransmits, some asymmetric RTTs.

sophia: ProviderX side shows repeated session resets. I already pulled their POC info. Opening ticket now.

jess: paging rota: mike is on-call network for this window, carla SRE for escalation. mike / carla please confirm if you want bridge.

mike: starting a quick bridge. dialing provider POC. bridge code 8342 (internal).

providerx-support: ProviderX acknowledges they observe instability on one of their backbone nodes in FRA region, investigating. Link-engineers assigned. We may see intermittent reachability while they flap peers.

carla: mitigation options discussed: 1) prepend/withdraw specific problematic prefixes from ProviderX temporarily, 2) shift traffic via BackupTransit (AS64520) by adjusting localpref and path prepends, 3) request ProviderX to dampen flaps or reset session.

alex: quick test: added temporary inbound route-preference to prefer BackupTransit for eu-west prefixes (local-pref bump). monitoring immediate impact.

sophia: note: backup path has slightly higher latency, but stable. we'll prefer stability for customer traffic.

carla: live impact update: after pref change at 14:25 UTC error rate fell from 22% -> 6% for affected services. Latency up ~20ms median. customer-impact: degraded but largely functional.

mike: continuing to coordinate with ProviderX. they asked for BGP neighbor debug dumps. sophia, can you paste full bgp summary + bgp flap counters?

sophia: pasted to bridge. gist of flap counters: 203.0.113.10 flaps=12, 203.0.113.11 flaps=15 in last 30m. they've requested we hold backup preference while they remediate.

providerx-support: update: we've identified a fabric config bug on their FRA POP causing session resets. patch rolling at 14:40 UTC, predicted 10-15m to converge. We recommend Hold-time increase and flap dampening enabled if you want to avoid reflare.

carla: decision: keep traffic on BackupTransit for 1 hour, monitor, and then slowly lean back when ProviderX confirms stable for 30m. Also enabling temporary BGP dampening isn't ideal for production but ok as short term.

alex: adding short incident note to postmortem: root cause upstream FRANKFURT fabric causing BGP session resets -> packet loss. mitigation: traffic shift to BackupTransit, ProviderX patch.

jess: notifying Customer Success for affected accounts and drafting initial incident message. severity: P2 currently due to partial region impact and degraded API.

mike: handing off to night on-call at 15:00 UTC. I'll leave monitoring hooks and runbook steps in the incident doc. carla will be primary SRE for follow-ups.

carla: I'll own the handoff. next steps: 1) confirm ProviderX stable for 30m, 2) revert local-pref change gradually, 3) run connectivity tests + SYN/ACK rate checks.

sophia: providerx-support: please post final confirmation once remediation deployed. we need timestamped event for postmortem.

providerx-support: remediation completed at 14:53 UTC; fabric patch applied and sessions re-established. Monitoring for 30m recommended.

carla: re-evaluating — as of 15:10 UTC sessions stable, no new flaps. will start slow revert to normal routing at 15:20 UTC.

alex: final customer impact summary for handoff: - Window: 14:06-15:20 UTC, primary impact until 14:25 when traffic shifted. - Affected region: eu-west - Customer-facing impact: increased errors and degraded streaming; mitigated by shift to BackupTransit, residual latency increase ~20ms. - Next: full postmortem and RCA.

mike: thanks team. handoff acknowledged. carla takes ownership. :white_check_mark:
